calls.reason: PromptBench (June 2023) backs the wording-sensitivity part. But no evidence here shows that training-data quirks drive commonsense performance, and 'illusion' and 'something missing' are too vague to call.

Bian et al. (March 2023) found ChatGPT below 70% on social, event and temporal commonsense sets. That is repeated failure across several domains, even though Bang et al. report strong results on small samples elsewhere.

Verma et al. (June 2023) used validated paraphrases with GPT-3 at temperature zero. Its predictions changed on about 9-14% of reworded items, so correctness shifted with wording. PromptBench found the same kind of sensitivity.
